state.case_summary:
A woman in her 40s with a medical history of infective endocarditis and hepatitis C secondary to ongoing intravenous drug use presented to the emergency department with severe back pain. She had recently undergone tricuspid valve replacement with a 29-mm bioprosthetic Carpentier-Edwards valve complicated by transient third-degree heart block. Two days after pacemaker placement, she experienced episodes of light-headedness and chest pain.

Blood pressure was 94/60 mm Hg. Heart rates were between 150 and 190 beats per minute.

- Electrocardiogram findings:    Image Title: Figure 1. Electrocardiogram During Tachycardia    Image Description: Shows P waves upright in leads II, III, and aVF with sinus rate of 96 beats per minute. Grouped beating pattern with 1 P wave producing 2 QRS complexes, creating a regularly irregular rhythm.      - Prior Imaging:    Transesophageal echocardiography revealed pulmonic valve vegetations and severe tricuspid valve regurgitation secondary to a flail leaflet.

root.label: Acute Cardiovascular instability with Severe Tachycardia and Hypotension
supporting_facts: Recent tricuspid valve replacement with bioprosthetic valve
Episodes of light-headedness and chest pain
Electrocardiogram showing grouped beating pattern with regularly irregular rhythm
Hypotension (BP 94/60 mmHg) and tachycardia (heart rate 150-190 beats per minute)
excluded_candidates: Pulmonary embolism: considered due to recent surgery and immobility, but less likely given the ECG findings
Myocardial infarction: considered due to chest pain, but less likely given the ECG findings and recent pacemaker placement
